Ying Wai (应伟) 45, Sushing, /un-

1939年7月12日凌晨1时45分，总部刑事科的一组侦探在协助日本领事警察时，突袭了派克路（Park Road）253弄41号，并查获了包括武器在内的若干物品，其中有一支德蒙（Demon）.32口径自动手枪，编号1306和719。经枪械鉴定科检验，确认该手枪即为本案中导致马育航（Moa Hyoh Jong）死亡所使用的凶器。该手枪已移交给日本领事警察。

1939年7月12日凌晨1时46分，另一组总部刑事科侦探协助日本领事警察，突袭了派克路29号，逮捕了一名男子：
应伟（Ying Wai），45岁，苏州人，无业

1939年7月12日凌晨3时30分，又一组总部刑事科侦探在法国警察的协助下，协助日本领事警察，突袭了瓦隆路（Route Vallon）142号，将以下人员拘留：
罗炎（Loh Yien），49岁，泰阳（Taiyang，音译）人，煤商

上述查获物品及逮捕行动的详细情况已在刑事科总部（刑事情报处）杂项档案 105/39 中全面列明。

两名被捕者均承认是反日组织的成员，并向副督察长宋平通（Soong Ping Tuoong，音译）及本人口头承认参与谋杀马业翁（Ma Nyeh Oong，音译），但日本领事警察当局不允许就此作出书面供词（参见刑事情报处杂项档案 105/39 日记第29页第1页）。

没有理由怀疑他们的供述是为了逃避被永久移交给日本领事警察，而这一移交实际上分别发生于1939年7月21日和1938年8月14日。

自那些日期以来，市警察局未收到关于日本领事当局对他们采取行动的任何报告。

鉴于已查获物证以及两人的供述（虽为口头），谨建议将此案视为已成功侦破。

Date 9 / 2 / 39

January 30, 1939. Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

MURDER IN SUN SUN HOTEL

At about 7 p.m. yesterday a murder took place in Room 605 of the Sun Sun Hotel, Kweichow Road, the victim being one Moo Yoch-hang (馬育航), an official of the "Reformed Government".

The murdered lodger, a man of about 50 years of age, frequently travels between Shanghai and Hongkong and when in Shanghai he always stays at the Sun Sun Hotel. For this reason, most of the room boys of the hotel know his surname as Moo.

About 5 or 6 days ago Moo booked Room 605 on the 5th floor, giving his name on the hotel register as Tsai (蔡). He never slept in the room; he used to call at the hotel either in the morning or afternoon and left at about midnight. At ordinary times he was visited by friends who kept their movements very secret. Most of his friends are well dressed. Apparently they called to make certain arrangements as no mahjongg games or other amusements were noticed.

At 9 a.m. yesterday Moo arrived at the room and locked himself in. Room boys entered the room on several occasions in answer to calls, but he seemed to have something on his mind. At 7 p.m. the room boys suddenly heard a noise like the firing of a pistol shot. They visited all the rooms to ascertain the location of the noise. When the boys went to Room 605 they saw Moo lying in front of the bath room with a bullet wound in the right temple. There was much blood on the floor and on a table. Judging by his dress, he seemed to have just risen from the bed and was shot while sitting at the table. The murderer left immediately after the crime. The door was found unlocked. The Louza Police was informed and the wounded man was removed to the Chinese Lester Hospital but died at 9.45 p.m.

A special pass bearing the photograph of the deceased in the name of Moo Yoch-hang, age 42, native of Fukien, Councillor to the "Reformed Government", was found in the room. The pass was signed by Wen Chung-yao, President of the Legislative Yuan of the "Reformed Government".

It is learned that Moo formerly held an important post under General Chen Chuin-ming (陳炯明). At one time he planned, on behalf of the Japanese, a revolt among the Chinese troops in Kwangtung so as to enable the Japanese to take the province without fighting. For his work he was given his present appointment. Recently, he became manager of a branch office of the "South China Rice Company". It is said that his death might be due to internal strife such as unequal division over spoils of office.

1939年1月30日。晨间译文

《标准报》及其他本地报纸：

新新饭店发生谋杀案

昨晚7时许，贵州路新新饭店605房间发生了一起谋杀案，受害者为“维新政府”官员马育航（Moo Yoch-hang）。

遇害的住客是一名约50岁的男子，经常往返于上海和香港之间，在上海时总是住在新新饭店。因此，饭店的大部分侍役都知道他姓马（Moo）。

大约五六天前，马以蔡（Tsai）为名在酒店登记簿上预订了五楼的605房间。他从未在房间内过夜；他通常在上午或下午来到酒店，并在午夜左右离开。平时有朋友来访，但行踪十分隐秘。他的朋友大多衣着考究。显然他们来访是为了商定某些安排，因为未发现有人打麻将或其他娱乐活动。

昨天上午9点，马来到房间并将自己锁在里面。侍役曾多次应呼叫进入房间，但他似乎心事重重。晚上7点，侍役们突然听到类似手枪射击的声音。他们查看了所有房间以确定声音来源。当侍役们来到605房间时，看到马躺在浴室前，右太阳穴有枪伤。地板上和桌子上有很多血。从他的衣着判断，他似乎刚起床，正坐在桌边时被枪击。凶手作案后立即离开。门被发现未上锁。警方接到通知，伤者被送往中式莱斯脱医院（Chinese Lester Hospital），但于晚上9点45分死亡。

在房间内发现了一张印有死者照片的特别通行证，姓名为马育航，42岁，福建人，“维新政府”顾问。该通行证由“维新政府”立法院院长温宗尧（Wen Chung-yao）签署。

据悉，马曾任陈炯明将军麾下的重要职务。他曾代表日本人策划广东中国军队的叛乱，以便日本人兵不血刃地占领该省。因这项工作，他获得了目前的任命。最近，他成为“华南米业公司”一家分公司的经理。据说他的死可能是由于内部争斗，例如对职位利益的分配不均所致。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JAN 31 1939

Murdered Man Was
Important Official

Moo Ngoh-hung Said to
Have Come from Nanking

Headquarters detectives of the
Shanghai Municipal Police yesterday
continued the investigation of the
assassination which took place on
Sunday evening on the sixth floor of
the Sun Sun Hotel, Nanking Road, a
case to which considerable importance
is attached.

The middle-aged victim, Moo Ngoh-
hung, was killed with one shot from
a pistol held by a man who entered
Moo's room alone and who managed
to escape after the crime. Moo is
reported to have been formerly the
Chief of the Finance Bureau of the
Kwangtung Provisional Government,
and at the time of his death was chief
adviser to the Executive Yuan of the
central "Reformed Government." He
had been staying in the Sun Sun
Hotel, which is situated above the Sun
Sun department store, since January
23. He is thought to have arrived
here from Nanking on a political
mission.

Despite Moo's connections with the
Japanese-sponsored régime, the mo-
tive for the assassination is not en-
tirely clear. Efforts are being made
to trace his past and to learn what
enemies he might have made.

By examination of the cartridge-
case the Police have established that
the pistol with which Moo was killed
was used in 1930 by a robber in the
West Hongkew district. The history
of the weapon is being further
scrutinized.

《字林西报》，

1939年1月31日

遇害者系
重要官员

据称马鄂洪（Moo Ngoh-hung，音译）
来自南京

上海公共租界工部局警务处总部侦探昨日继续调查周日晚发生在南京路新新饭店六楼的暗杀案，此案备受重视。

中年受害者马鄂洪（Moo Ngoh-hung）被一名独自进入其房间的男子用手枪开一枪击中身亡，该男子作案后成功逃脱。据报道，马曾任广东省临时政府财政局局长，遇害时担任中央“维新政府”行政院首席顾问。自1月23日以来，他一直住在位于新新百货公司楼上的新新饭店。据信他是带着政治使命从南京来到此地的。

尽管马与日本扶植的政权有联系，但暗杀的动机尚不完全清楚。警方正努力追溯其过往，以了解他可能结下了哪些仇敌。

通过对弹壳的检查，警方确定杀害马的手枪曾于1930年被虹口西区的一名劫匪使用过。该武器的历史正在进一步审查中。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

JAN 31 1939

Murdered Man
Identified As
Puppet Leader

Wealth Said Amassed
By Aiding Japanese
In South China

Mystery yesterday continued to shroud the killing of Mo Ngyoh-hung, one-time a high official in the Kwangtung Provincial Government, who died yesterday of a bullet wound in the head in a local hotel.

A Chinese report indicated that from the belongings of the murdered man, it has been unmistakably established that he was connected with the Nanking puppet regime. His identification card, signed by Wen Tsung-yao, the puppet "Legislative Yuan" chief, was issued by the "Provisional Government."

Arriving in the city on January 23, Mo registered in the hotel under the assumed name of Tsai. He told the hotel management that he had just arrived from Hongkong.

Another Chinese report stated that Mo had actively co-operated with the Japanese authorities in Canton shortly after they captured the southern city. It was reported that Mo had "cleaned up" several lakhs in this enterprise before he returned to Shanghai.

Before taking part in the Japanese-sponsored regime, Mo held several important government posts. At one time, he was Commissioner of Finance in Kwangtung Province while at a later date, he served as a committeeman of the Military Affairs Council of the National Government.

The murderer is still at large but the police are in possession of his finger prints.

《大美晚报》。

1939年1月31日

遇害者
被确认为
傀儡头目

据称其财富系
在华南协助日本人
所积聚

昨天，马岳洪（Mo Ngyoh-hung，音译）之死仍笼罩在谜团之中。马曾是广东省政府的高级官员，昨日在当地一家旅馆因头部枪伤死亡。

一份中文报道指出，从遇害者的遗物中，已明确证实他与南京傀儡政权有关联。他的身份证由傀儡“立法院”院长温宗尧（Wen Tsung-yao）签署，由“临时政府”签发。

马于1月23日抵达本市，在酒店登记时使用了化名“蔡”。他告诉酒店管理层他刚从香港抵达。

另一份中文报道指出，在日本人占领广州这座南方城市后不久，马曾积极与日本当局合作。据报道，马在此项活动中“捞取”了数十万巨款，随后返回上海。

在参与日本扶植的政权之前，马曾担任多个重要的政府职务。他曾一度担任广东省财政厅长，后来还担任过国民政府军事委员会的委员。

凶手仍在逃，但警方掌握着他的指纹。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 31 1939

Mystery
Shrouds
Shooting

Police Have Record Of
Pistol Used In Sun
Sun Hotel Murder

Mystery yesterday continued to
shroud the brutal murder in the
Sun-Sun Hotel on Sunday evening
of a middle-aged Chinese, reported
to be a high official of the City
Government of Nanking. Detectives
of the Crime Branch Headquarters
of the Shanghai Municipal Police
are in charge of investigations, but
up to late yesterday had not been
able to unravel anything of im-
portance.

The only clue left in the room in
which Mr. Mao Yu-ong, 45, was
found shot through the head, an
empty cartridge, was identified by
ballistic experts of the Shanghai
Municipal Police as having been
fired from a pistol, which had been
seized by the S.M.P. in 1930. The
weapon was confiscated by the
First Special District Court. What
happened to the pistol after that,
the police had not ascertained yes-
terday.

The son of the murdered man was
located by detectives yesterday. He
expressed great surprise at hearing
that his father was in Shanghai.
The son informed the police that
his father had not been in Shang-
hai for several years and that he
did not know what he had been
doing during the past two years.
Formerly, he said, his father was
connected with the National Gov-
ernment.

It was rumoured in Chinese
circles yesterday that the deceased
held the position of Secretary-
General of the Nanking City Gov-
ernment. In his possession the
police found a Japanese laissez-
passer.

The task of the police in track-
ing down the murderer is made
difficult due to the fact that no one
saw him arrive at the hotel or de-
part The roomboy heard a shot
whilst he was in another room and
on rushing into the one occupied
by Mr. Mao found him lying dead
on the floor.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。

1939年1月31日

谜团
笼罩
枪击案

警方存有
新新饭店谋杀案
所用枪支记录

昨天，周日晚在新新饭店发生的一起中年华人被残忍谋杀的案件仍笼罩在谜团之中，据报道该华人是南京市政府的高级官员。上海公共租界工部局警务处总部刑事科的侦探负责调查，但直到昨天深夜仍未理清任何重要线索。

在毛玉翁（Mao Yu-ong，音译），45岁，被发现头部中枪身亡的房间内留下的唯一线索是一枚空弹壳，上海公共租界工部局警务处的弹道专家鉴定该弹壳是由一支手枪发射的，该手枪曾于1930年被工部局警务处查获。该武器已被第一特区法院没收。至于那支手枪此后下落如何，警方昨天尚未查明。

侦探们昨天找到了遇害者的儿子。他对听到父亲在上海的消息表示非常惊讶。儿子告知警方，他的父亲已有数年不在上海，且他不知道父亲在过去两年里一直在做什么。他说，父亲以前曾与国民政府有关联。

昨天在华界圈子里流传着一种说法，称死者担任南京市政府秘书长一职。警方在他身上发现了一张日本通行证。

由于无人看到凶手抵达或离开酒店，警方追踪凶手的任务变得困难重重。侍役在另一个房间时听到了一声枪响，冲进毛先生居住的房间时，发现他已倒在地板上身亡。

1939年1月29日，在“维新政府”行政院首席顾问马育航（Mau Yoh Ong）（Ma Yoh Heng）遇刺后，于贵州路孙孙饭店（Sun Sun Hotel）605房间发现的文件及其他物品清单。

在死者身上发现

1) 名片：-

(a) 以梁鸿志（Liang Hung-ts）（注：“维新政府”行政院院长）名义印制的名片，背面用中文写有以下附注：-

"75 Kwoh Hwa Road(國華路), undertaking the

Please visit 3rd floor, 22 Kwoh Hwa Road to

2) Manuscript bearing the heading, "Matters to be dealt with
in South China." This document contains rough notes
relating to (a) Preparations for the establishment of a
new political rule in Kwangtung, (b) Intelligence work
along the Shanghai-Nanking line, (c) Intelligence work
in Kwangtung and Kwangsi, (d) Press propaganda to be
conducted in Hongkong on behalf of the "Central China
Government. The expenses for press propaganda in Hongkong
are estimated at $50,000 to $150,000.
(Translation of this document will be made).

3) Manuscript bearing the heading "General Enquiries".
It states that investigations will be made into the
following matters:- General situation, education, economics,
finance, pacification work, and industries.
(Translation of this document will be made).

4) A note paper containing the following notes written in
pencil:-
" (1) Transfers and locations of independent brigades
of various divisions of the 4th Route Army.
(2) Plans for 'Provincial Defence.'
(3) Can the Central Government Army enter Kwangtung?
(4) The 'political' relations between Kwangtung and
the Central Government.
(5) Air bases. The number and type of airplanes, and
the location of aerodromes.
(6) The defence works in Kwangtung. "

5) A sheet of paper containing the following penciled notes:-
" In the back row,
No. 3 Sz Yeong Kung(史詠賡).
No. 4 Moh Ying Liang(馬良).
No. 6 Zung Kung Yah (陈庚雅).

6) Letter dated January 11, addressed to "Brother Yok" (the
deceased) from Chi( 寄 ) stating that it does appear that
Waung Ching Wei has made arrangements before his departure
from Chungking, and that many difficulties have to be
encountered before the matter can be accomplished, etc.
(Translation of this letter will be made.)

7) Manuscript entitled "General Principles of Organization
of the 'Boxing Expedition Group' (拳討团) of X X Party".
According to this document, the group will be organized
in Hongkong and Kowloon for the purpose of dealing with
"reactionaries" by means of "iron and blood".
(Translation of this document will be made).

8) Manuscript entitled "General Principles of Organization
of X X News Agency." According to this document, the
news agency will be established for the purpose of
supplying news materials to the newspaper offices in
Hongkong and abroad.
(Translation of this document will be made).

9) Three receipts issued by the Canton City Bank during 1934,
to Mr. Moh Tsi Zung(马齐成) for monies received in
repayment of a loan. One for $1,400, the second for
$2,000 and the third for $600.

10) A receipt, dated 1930, issued by Woo Kwung Foo(吴光圃)
to Moh Yoh Hong (the deceased) for $1,400 in Kwangtung
currency, stating that the money will be refunded in 50 days.

2) 标题为“华南待办事项”的手稿。该文件包含有关以下内容的粗略笔记：(a) 在广东建立新政治统治的准备工作，(b) 沪宁沿线的情报工作，(c) 广东和广西的情报工作，(d) 代表“华中政府”在香港进行的新闻宣传。在香港进行新闻宣传的费用估计为5万至15万美元。
（将翻译此文件）。

3) 标题为“一般查询”的手稿。其中声明将对以下事项进行调查：- 总体局势、教育、经济、财政、绥靖工作及工业。
（将翻译此文件）。

4) 一张便笺纸，上面用铅笔写有以下笔记：-
“ (1) 第四路军各师独立旅的调动及驻地。
(2) ‘省防’计划。
(3) 中央政府军队能否进入广东？
(4) 广东与中央政府之间的‘政治’关系。
(5) 空军基地。飞机的数量和类型，以及机场的位置。
(6) 广东的防御工事。”

3号 史咏赓（Sz Yeong Kung）。

6号 陈庚雅（Zung Kung Yah）。”

6) 1月11日的信件，由Chi（寄）写给“Yok兄”（死者），信中指出，汪精卫在离开重庆前似乎已做出安排，且在事情完成之前会遇到许多困难等。
（将翻译此信。）

7) 题为“XX党‘拳讨团’组织通则”的手稿。根据该文件，该团将在香港和九龙组建，目的是通过“铁与血”的手段对付“反动派”。
（将翻译此文件）。

8) 题为“XX通讯社组织通则”的手稿。根据该文件，成立该通讯社的目的是向香港及海外的报社提供新闻素材。
（将翻译此文件）。

(周之楨) on letter papers and envelopes of the Kowloon

(a) addressed to "brother Foo( 古 )" (address not given),
dated November 7, requesting the addressee to discuss
on various matters with Moh Yeh Hong (the deceased)
"who will visit Shanghai to offer his services in
rehabilitation work."

(b) addressed to Zah Gee Ziang(石祺祥),"Business Dept.
of Telephone Co.," dated November 6, requesting the
addressee to render all possible assistance to Mah

29) Draft of a contract between a Chinese business concern
and a Japanese firm (names not given) relating to shipping
trade along the Yangtse.

written on note papers of the Hwa Hwee Trading Company,
Shanghai Office; 221 Foochow Road; Hongkong office, 48
Koshing Street.

( 罗武 )", dated Jan. 13 and 21, respectively, dealing
dealing with a case of private civil prosecution.

32) Letter dated "28th", signed Liang( 良 ), addressed to
Cheu Tien Yui( 丘天羽 ), 7 Tai Bing Ka, Sie Koong Mung,
Peiping, dealing with the conditions or whereabouts of
certain friends. The letter paper and envelope of the
Sun Sun Hotel were used.
(Translation of this letter will be made).

33) Letter dated "Jan. 27th", signed Yoong( 庸 ), addressed
to Ts( 芝 ) (address not given) to the effect that the
addresser has been in Shanghai for about twenty days
and has not yet decided as to which side he will join
pending investigations into the conditions at various
places. Sun Sun Hotel letter paper used.

34) Letter dated Jan. 1, addressed by one Yuen( 阮 ) in
Hongkong to Mah Tse Liang( 李子良 ), c/o Tsai Tsung Hwa
( 蔡正華 ), Tai Ziang Co. ( 泰祥 ), 521, Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road, Shanghai. A translation reads as follows:-
"Uncle Liang,
Your letter has been received, and the enclosed letter
has been handed to uncle Hao( 浩 ). Some one has arrived
in Hongkong and has been told not to be in a hurry.
Mr. Zung ( 鄭 ) of Macao has not come and the matter has
to be suspended. Zuh and I have nothing to do with
Iiu( 刘 ) and Su( 苏 ). We are waiting for your
instructions regarding this matter. Tso Dien( 竹康 ).

page_data.en:
Translation of Exhibit 6.

Letter dated January 11, addressed to
"Brother Yoh" (the deceased) from Chi (寄).

January 11.

Brother Yoh:

I am in receipt of the two letters you sent
me and I quite agree with your opinion and views. I
have never been anxious at securing money and therefore
there should be no concern about eating my own words.
She (he) is not known to have been fond of criticizing
others. What You Tse (茂之) has to say is far more
unreliable.

It does not seem to be the case that
Japan is very anxious to sue for peace. We should
carefully examine the information emanating from
various sources. I wish to be informed of the news, if
any, that you may hear from your interviews with Ching
(钦) and Lan (兰).

It does not appear that Wang Ching-wei has
made arrangements before his forced departure from
Chungking. Many difficulties will be encountered before
the matter can be accomplished. No telegram has been
received from Brother Tai (岱).

Some new ways may be found for the affairs
over here. You will be acquainted with the progress
in further communications.

Chi (寄).

1 月 11 日。

幼兄：

我收到了你寄给我的两封信，我完全同意你的意见和观点。我从不急于求财，因此不必担心我会食言。他（她）向来不以批评他人著称。茂之 (You Tse) 所说的话更不可靠。

日本似乎并不急于求和。我们应该仔细审查来自各种渠道的信息。如果你从与钦 (Ching) 和兰 (Lan) 的会谈中听到任何消息，希望能告知我。

汪精卫在被迫离开重庆之前似乎并未做好安排。此事在完成之前会遇到许多困难。尚未收到岱兄 (Brother Tai) 的电报。

寄 (Chi)。

2. 宗旨：本团体将按照 XX 党特务部的命令行事，执行以武力对付反动派的“铁血”政策。

3. 地址：不定。

4. 组织：本团体设指挥官一名，秘书一名，七个“区队”，以及一个机动队。每个区队设队长一名及队员若干名。香港和九龙划分为七个区，每个区分配一个“区队”，具体如下：-
区。

第二区队：湾仔、鹅颈及跑马地。

大多数重要政府官员居住在大坑道。
第四区队：尖沙咀、红磡及邮船码头。
第五区队：油麻地、旺角及码头。

Draft of a contract between a Chinese
business concern and a Japanese firm
(names not given) relating to shipping
trade along the Yangtze.

The business concern as Party A.
The Japanese firm as Party B.

1) Party B shall be responsible for acquiring the right
of navigation along the Yantse and for completing
all other relevant arrangements.

2) All negotiations between Party A and the Japanese
authorities in connection with the trade of Party
A shall be undertaken by Party B.

3) The business of Party A shall not be interfered with
by Party B but the accounts of Party A may be subject
to examination from time to time by an auditor to be
detailed by Party B.

4) Should it become necessary for Party A to establish
branches in the various ports along the Yangtsze
River, such as Hankow, Kiukiang, Nanking and Wuhu
etc., Party A may request Party B to detail a certain
number of capable hands to be resident at the ports
for the purpose of taking charge of negotiations that
might arise between Party A and the local Japanese
authorities. The business of Party A shall not be
interfered with by men detailed by Party B.

5) After deducting all expenses, X X tenth of the net
profit which accrues from the Party A shall be given
to Party B. A bi-monthly return of all accounts
shall be made, by Party A.

6) The trade of Party A shall be limited to the
transportation and sale of native products along the
Yangtsze all other sundry foreign goods and
contraband shall be prohibited.

一家中国商号与一家日本公司（名称未具）之间关于长江航运贸易的合同草案。

该商号为甲方。
该日本公司为乙方。

1) 乙方应负责取得长江航行权，并完成所有其他相关安排。

2) 甲方与日本当局之间有关甲方贸易的所有谈判，均由乙方承担。

3) 乙方不得干涉甲方的业务，但乙方可指派一名审计员不时审查甲方的账目。

4) 若甲方有必要在汉口、九江、南京和芜湖等长江沿线各港口设立分支机构，甲方可要求乙方派遣若干能干人员常驻各港口，负责处理甲方与当地日本当局之间可能出现的谈判事宜。乙方派遣的人员不得干涉甲方的业务。

5) 扣除所有费用后，甲方所得净利润的十分之X应给予乙方。甲方应每两个月提交一次所有账目的报表。

6) 甲方的贸易仅限于长江沿线土特产的运输和销售，禁止经营其他各类外国商品及违禁品。

"28th"

To-day I am in receipt of the letter dated
January 3, from Hongkong, to which city the letter had
originally been despatched. The contents of this
letter are enumerated below:-

1) Yui Lao ( 瑜老 ) and Pah Wei ( 伯偉 ) etc., have
deserted us and gone over to the side of the
leftists.

2) Tah Tsai ( 達材 ) is at present residing with his
employer at the Nanking Bank in Hongkong. The
Chairman of the Board of Directors is quite well
off. We are as poor as ever and seldom see him,
except when meeting him in the street.

3) I have forgotten the address of Ying Wu ( 英武 ),
but letters may be despatched to the home of Woo
Siao-ming ( 吳小銘 ), Sung Chong, Yung Sung Street,
Hongkong, where he is residing. It appears that
he is holding the position of an office assistant
in the employ of one named Wong ( 黃 ), who is his
fellow-provincial. I saw him very often in Hongkong
and I find that he is not opposed to any activities
in which we may take part.

4) Sz Yah ( 師爺 ) and Tung Yuan ( 東園 ) etc., do not
amount to anything, and that is part of my reason
for leaving Hongkong, since it would not be fair if
I should refuse him my cooperation. He is not in
the money at present, yet he advocates radical steps
being taken, which I am not in favour.

1939年1月29日在贵州路孙孙饭店605房间发现的文件清单中第32号证物的译文。

署名为“良”，日期为“28日”，致北平西公永大盛街7号丘天友的信函译文。

“28日”

今日收到一封发自香港、原寄往该地的1月3日来信。该信内容列举如下：-

1) 瑜老和伯伟等人已背离我们，转投左派阵营。

2) 达材目前与其雇主居住在香港的南京银行。董事长家境颇为富裕。我们依然如故般贫困，除了在街上偶遇外，很少见到他。

3) 我忘记了英武的地址，但信件可寄至香港永胜街宋冲吴小铭家中，他现居于此。看来他在为一位名叫黄的同乡任职，担任办公室助理一职。我在香港常常见到他，发现他对我们要参与的任何活动并不反对。

4) 师爷和东园等人不成气候，这也是我离开香港的部分原因，因为如果我拒绝与他合作，似乎有失公允。他目前手头并不宽裕，却主张采取激进措施，对此我并不赞成。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

5) The employer of Shiang Chi (香池 ) has already
assumed the post of Deputy-Chief at the native
country of Tseu Sz Yah (周師爺). Nothing can be
done in this direction. Li Ngo (李吾 ) has made
some unsuccessful endeavours at persuasion and has
incurred an expense of from $1,000 to $2,000.
6) Relatives of Li Ngo have often held conversations
with us. I do not agree with his methods which are
far from being thorough. My opinion is that a sum
should be set aside specially for the project.
7) I may have to stay for some time yet.
8) It is rather insecure to reside in Hongkong, since
a World War is likely to break out at any moment.
But what can we do if we have no money, even for
removal.
I have rarely communicated with Tseu Sz Yah,
who is a bore to me. If you should see him, just give
him my regards.

Liang ( 良 ).
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

5) 香池的雇主已在周师爷的家乡就任副职首长。在此方向上已无能为力。李吾曾尝试劝说但未成功，并花费了1,000至2,000元。
6) 李吾的亲属常与我们交谈。我不同意他的方法，因为这些方法远不够彻底。我的意见是，应为该项目专门拨出一笔款项。
7) 我可能还需停留一段时间。
8) 居住在香港相当不安全，因为世界大战随时可能爆发。但如果我们连搬迁的费用都没有，又能怎么办呢？
我很少与周师爷联系，他令我感到厌烦。如果你见到他，代我向他问好。

良。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 9 p.m. 29.1.39, as result of a communication received from Supt. Mason, D.D.O."A", the undersigned accompanied by D.S. Fowler and C.D.S. 274, attended Louza Station in connection with this case and as result of a perusal of a note book found on person of the deceased one named Chen Ping Tsun (陳炳蓀) residing 68 Great Western Road was communicated with, first by telephone, and later in person at the aforesaid address. This gentleman when questioned regarding the deceased, stated that about 15 years ago he had met this man, i.e. Mau Yoh Ong (馬友航) age 59, native of Canton, whilst the latter was chief of the Administration of Finance of the Provincial Government of Kwangtung, and that since then he had remained on friendly terms with this man. Continuing Mr. Chen explained that in recent years the deceased had given up his political career and had taken up business with the South China Rice Trading Co. in Hongkong. Further questioned regarding the arrival of the deceased in Shanghai on this occasion and his reasons for coming here, Mr. Chen, explained that he knew nothing definite in this direction, but that approximately three weeks ago, the deceased had called at his home

At 7.06 p.m. 29-1-39, a telephone message was
received at Louisa Station from the Sun Sun Hotel
(新新旅館) Kweichow Road, reporting that a man had
been shot in Room 605 of the hotel.

Officer i/c of Station, D.I. Bennett, D.S.I.
Raiders and detectives immediately attended.

Room 605 of this hotel is situated on the 6th
floor of the hotel, to which access may be gained
either by stairway or lift, the lift however only
proceeding to the 5th floor, when access to the 6th
floor must be gained by the stairway, room 605 being
situated a considerable distance from top of stair-
way of this floor.

Upon arrival at room 605, the body of a male
Chinese was found lying on his back in a large pool
of blood, he having been wounded in the right side
of the face, directly in front of the right ear, he
being in an unconscious condition but still living.

The Fire Brigade Ambulance was called and the
injured male conveyed to the Lester Hospital, where
death ensued at 9.30 p.m. resultant from this bullet
wound, at no time did the now deceased regain
consciousness.

From enquiries it was ascertained that the now
deceased occupied room 605 on the 23-1-39 together
with three other male Chinese speaking Northern
dialect.

This room was registered in the name of Tsar (蔡)
by the now deceased, who has been the only occupant
of this room since this date, he however being visit-
ed daily by five or six men, all speaking northern

1939年1月29日晚上7:06，老闸巡捕房接到来自贵州路新新旅館（Sun Sun Hotel）的电话消息，报告该旅馆605室有一名男子被枪击。

巡捕房主管督察员贝内特（D.I. Bennett），副督察员。
突击队员及侦探立即赶赴现场。

该旅馆605室位于旅馆六楼，可通过楼梯或电梯到达，但电梯仅至五楼，因此必须通过楼梯才能到达六楼，而605室距离该楼层楼梯口相当远。

到达605室后，发现一名中国男性尸体仰面躺在一大滩血泊中，其右脸右耳正前方受伤，处于昏迷状态但仍存活。

呼叫了消防队救护车，将该受伤男子送往莱斯德医院（Lester Hospital），当晚9:30因该枪伤死亡，死者在此期间从未恢复意识。

经查询获悉，现死者于1939年1月23日与其他三名讲北方方言的中国男子共同入住605室。

该房间由现死者以蔡（Tsar）之名登记，自该日起他是该房间的唯一住客，但他每天接待五六名男子来访，这些人均讲北方

At about 6.00 p.m. 29-1-39, the room boy of this room took the bill into the room, which bill is presented every three days, this bill including telephone calls, etc. amounting to $42.30, the now deceased being the only occupant at this period, the bill being left on the table by the room boy (Wong Ching Kung (汪錦垣) Boy 56) who then left the room and was not aware of the shooting until he over-heard the number one boy telephoning to Louza Station reporting the occurrence (Statement 1).

Another room boy, one Liang Gue Ching (梁健青) No.41, states that whilst he was attending to the occupants of room 607, which is situated directly opposite to room 605, he heard what he thought was a shot fired from outside this room, and upon proceeding to the corridor saw that the door of room 605 was open and the male occupant lying on the floor, he then informed the number one boy who telephoned to the Station, he making no attempt to enter the room (Statement 2).

No attempt was made to raise any alarm, no person seen by this room boy to leave the room.

Enquiries by detectives fail to find any persons from amongst the hotel staff who may have seen any person leave the room or corridor where this room is situated.

This is corroborated by the position of the chair, bullet wound on right of the face of deceased, position of blood on the table, the deceased falling on his back to the floor, which all tend to point that the shot was fired from just inside the room, near to entrance of door-way.

Upon the table of this room was a book, printed in Chinese, the title however being in English, the title of which was "Mussolini".

在靠近床的地方发现一枚.32口径的空弹壳，床位于房间入口右侧；而从房间内桌子的位置来看，几乎正对着门口，看来现死者当时要么正坐在桌前写字，要么在阅读，很可能是在写字，因为在他尸体附近的地板上发现了一支毛笔，而桌上有墨汁，袭击者从刚进入房间门口的地方开枪并立即逃离，因为服务员梁健青发现该房间的大门是开着的（陈述2）。

椅子的位置、死者面部右侧的枪伤、桌上血迹的位置、死者仰面倒地等情形均佐证了这一点，这些都指向枪击是从刚进入房间门口附近实施的。

房间桌上有一本中文印刷的书，但标题是英文，书名为《墨索里尼》（"Mussolini"）。

对现死者的人身搜查发现一张日本签发的“通行证”，姓名为马育航（Ma Ngoh Hong），有效期至1939年4月30日，用于进入南京、虹口及江湾地区，注明此人为维新政府行政院顾问

CHINA PRESS.

JAN 30 1939

Mystery Man
Murdered In
Local Hotel

Dead Man Believed To
Have Been Puppet
Official

FOUND DEAD WITH
BULLET IN BRAIN

Victim Said Secretary
Of “Nanking City,
Government”

For the first time in weeks, another political assassination occurred in the International Settlement last night.
The dead man is Mo Ngyoh-hung, believed to be about 46 years of age. Although definite confirmation was lacking at press time, he is reported to have been the secretary of the Japanese sponsored “Nanking Municipal Government.”
Mo was shot to death by persons unknown while in his room at the Sun Sun Hotel on Nanking Road.

Boy Heard Shot
Shortly after 7 p.m., a room-boy in the hotel heard a shot which sounded as though it might have been fired in Mo’s room. Badly frightened, he called the hotel manager. The manager immediately called the Louza Police Station and Detective Inspector George Bennett took charge of the investigation.
Upon entering the room, the detectives found Mo stretched out on the floor, with a bullet hole in his brain. After detectives had completed their preliminary investigation on the spot, the body was sent to the Lester Chinese Hospital where it was pronounced dead.

Arrived January 21
Mo, as near as could be ascertained last night, arrived in Shanghai from Nanking on January 21 and proceeded to the Sun Sun Hotel where he took a room, registering under the name of Tsai.

He was an uncommunicative individual and gave none of the hotel employees an inkling as to what his business **〔此处转录不清〕** was not discovered until after his death that he was known in most circles in which he traveled as Mo Ngyoh-hung. The police are not even sure that this was his real name.

Political Connections
The preliminary investigation last night also turned up enough evidence to cause the authorities to believe that the man had definite political connections with the Japanese sponsored regime in the Central China area.
One report on the subject was to the effect that he had been connected with the “Nanking Municipal Government” for some time. Another report states that he also held the concurrent post of adviser to the “Shanghai City Government” and, hence, spent some of his time commuting between here and Nanking.
Just who might have been responsible for the killing is a matter that is puzzling the police as well as the hotel management. Employees of the hotel saw no suspicious characters enter Mo’s room, nor did they see anyone leave after the shooting.

神秘男子
在本市旅馆
被谋杀

死者据信曾为
傀儡官员

脑部中弹
身亡

受害者据称为
“南京市政府”秘书

数周以来，公共租界昨晚再次发生政治暗杀事件。
死者为莫雄（Mo Ngyoh-hung），据信约46岁。虽然截至发稿时尚无确切证实，但据报道他是日本扶植的“南京市政府”的秘书。
莫在南京路的新新旅馆房间内被不明身份者枪杀。

侍者听到枪声
晚上7点后不久，旅馆的一名侍者听到一声枪响，听起来像是从莫的房间发出的。他惊恐万分，随即叫来旅馆经理。经理立即致电老闸捕房，由侦探督察乔治·贝内特（George Bennett）负责调查。
侦探进入房间后，发现莫仰面躺在地板上，脑部有一个弹孔。侦探在现场完成初步调查后，尸体被送往莱斯德华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital），在那里被宣布死亡。

1月21日抵达
据昨晚尽可能查明的情况，莫于1月21日从南京抵达上海，随后前往新新旅馆开房，登记姓名为蔡（Tsai）。

他是一个沉默寡言的人，未向任何旅馆员工透露其业务**〔此处转录不清〕**直到他死后才被发现，他在其涉足的大多数圈子里被称为莫雄（Mo Ngyoh-hung）。警方甚至不确定这是否是他的真名。

政治背景
昨晚的初步调查还发现了足够的证据，使当局相信该人与华中地区日本扶植的政权有明确的政治联系。
有关此事的一份报告称，他与“南京市政府”已有段时间的联系。另一份报告称，他还兼任“上海市政府”顾问，因此部分时间在上海和南京之间往返。
究竟谁可能对这起杀人案负责，是让警方和旅馆管理层都感到困惑的问题。旅馆员工没有看到可疑人物进入莫的房间，也没有看到枪击后有人离开。

THE MURDER IN THE SUN SUN HOTEL

The remains of Mo Yoch-hang ( 馬育航 ), who was murdered on the evening of January 29 at the Sun Sun Hotel ( 新新旅館 ), were removed to the mortuary on Kiaochow Road at 8 a.m. yesterday. After a post-mortem examination had been held by the doctor of the Shanghai First Special District Court, Mo Sz-zee ( 馬思奇 ), a son of the deceased, identified the dead body. At noon yesterday the body was removed to the World Funeral Directors ( 普安殯儀館 ) on Kiaochow Road.

The remains will be encoffined at 2 p.m. to-day and will be kept there until arrangements have been made for removal to Mo's native place for burial.

It is learned that following the murder of Mo Yoch-hang, some Japanese in plain clothes called at the Police Station the same evening to make enquiries. They appeared to be much concerned over the affair.

The Police are continuing their investigations into the murder.

新新旅馆谋杀案

1月29日晚在新新旅馆被谋杀的马育航（Mo Yoch-hang）的遗体，于昨日上午8时被运往胶州路殡仪馆。经上海第一特区地方法院法医进行尸检后，死者之子马思奇（Mo Sz-zee）辨认了尸体。昨日中午，尸体被运往胶州路的普安殡仪馆。

遗体将于今天下午2时入殓，并将停灵于此，直至安排妥当运回马的家乡安葬。

据悉，马育航被谋杀后，当晚有几名便衣日本人前往捕房查询。他们似乎对此事非常关切。

警方正在继续调查这起谋杀案。

Sir,
I beg to report that at 2-30 p.m. 30/1/39 a telephone message was received from Mr. P.M. Streit of the Shanghai Telephone Co. to the effect that a Chinese member of his staff, who wished to remain anonymous, was willing to give certain information which might have a bearing on this case.

On receipt of this message, D.S. Fowler immediately proceeded to the office of Mr. Streit, and there met a male chinese, native of Formosa, who volunteered the following information:-

It would appear that in 1918, the informant, who was then employed in Government service, with the Kwangtung Provincial Government, came to know the deceased, who was then Chief of the Ministry of Finance, both working directly under General Chen Chui Ming (陈炯明) who was at that time Governor of Swatow, and that the deceased at this time was on very friendly terms with one named Tsai Cheng Jen (蔡祥生) who was known to be a close associate of Mr. Wang Ching Wei (汪精衛). Later as a result of an upheavel in the government caused through General Chen Chui Ming (陈炯明), all were forced to give up their respective positions, more so the deceased and Tsai Cheng Jen (蔡祥生), who were forced to flee the country, owing to warrants being issued for their arrest. Both these men fled to Japan, and remained there for some considerable time, Tsai Cheng Jen (蔡祥生), as result of entering Tokoy University remaining there the longest. Between that time and the present, both these men had held various Government positions, and four years ago the deceased was made an Honorary Counseller of the Military Affairs Commission of the Nationalist Government. The other man, i.e. Tsai Cheng Jen (蔡祥生), was however less fortunate, and for sometime prior to the outbreak of the present Sino-Japanese hostilities was being supported by the

当晚该旅馆的情况得到了线人的证实，他称在1939年1月29日晚上约9点，他接到蔡（Tsai）的电话，蔡告知他，当晚约8点，他曾偕同妻子前往新新旅馆（Sun Sun Hotel）六楼，但看到那里聚集着数名外籍警员，便向一名侍者询问发生了什么事，得知605房间的住客刚刚被刺杀后，他迅速离开，并将此事报告给日本特务机关，随后他与线人联系，要求线人扮演死者的儿子，以便在次日的验尸听证会上认领尸体。线人拒绝这样做，蔡（Tsai）随即表示他会找其他人来做这件事。

这位线人表现出非常愿意协助警方，接着被问及为何死者被要求来到上海，以及他是否能透露任何特殊原因，他回答说，虽然没有确凿证据，但他强烈怀疑在南方拥有相当多追随者的死者，与广州沦陷于日本人之手一事有关；鉴于死者在汕头及其周边地区仍有更强的影响力，日本人要求他前来上海可能是出于类似的原因，不过正如前一种情况一样，他对此没有确凿证据，只是表达他的怀疑。

由于此人做出上述披露显得颇为奇怪，尤其是当他声称自己是死者家属的挚友时，警方就此对他进行了谨慎的盘问，结果查明他这样做的原因是收到了一封

Fowler immediately returned to headquarters, where he informed
the undersigned, who in turn questioned the male Chinese in ques-
tion. This man still adhered to original statement to the effect
that he was the eldest son of the deceased, however when requested
to produce some means of identification he could not so, and re-
quested permission to return to his home in the French Concession
where he could definitely identify himself. As mentioned in Diary No.2
of this file he did so to the satisfaction of all concerned.

of all documents etc found in possession of the deceased, a per-
usal of which in no small way confirms the information as given
by this informer, and tends to show that the deceased was undoubt-

来自死者在香港的妻子的电报，请求他协助安排葬礼，他担心蔡（Tsai）以及日本当局可能会干涉此事。随后向他解释，在当天上午的验尸听证会上，一名自称是死者儿子的中国男子认领了尸体，而此人目前就在警察总局。线人解释说这不可能，因为据他所知，死者的家庭成员均不在上海，为了证实这一点，他复述了蔡祥生（Tsai Cheng Jen）的话，蔡曾 stated 说他会找其他人来冒充死者的儿子。

鉴于这后一条信息，副督察福勒（D.S. Fowler）立即返回总局，向本人通报了情况，本人随即讯问了该名中国男子。该男子仍坚持原来的说法，即他是死者的长子，然而当要求他出示某种身份证明时，他无法做到，并请求允许返回他在法租界的家中，以便能够确切地证明自己的身份。正如本档案日记第2号中所述，他这样做了，并令所有相关方满意。

随函附上在死者身上发现的所有文件等的译文副本，查阅这些文件在很大程度上证实了该线人所提供的信息，并倾向于表明死者无疑在为日本特务科从事获取情报的工作。

MG.                     此致，

                        您顺从的仆人。

                        约翰·克拉彭（John Clapham）
